strengths: Novel insight that citation consistency across permutations is a more stable aggregation signal than answer text frequency — well-motivated and testable
Training-free design makes CCV practically deployable without model access, filling a clear gap between the two existing categories
Specific quantitative claims (+0.19 SubEM, p = 1.14e-5) lend some credibility to the empirical grounding
Clear positioning against prior work (Stable-RAG, Mixture-of-Agents) with honest articulation of their limitations
weaknesses: Evaluation is limited to a single dataset (NaturalQuestions); generalizability to other QA tasks, domains, or long-form generation is undemonstrated
The +0.19 SubEM improvement is modest and may not be practically significant; no error bars or statistical significance for the primary metric are reported
Method assumes models reliably produce grounded citations, which is not guaranteed — the 'evidence validity' filtering step is underspecified and may itself introduce noise
Only compared against majority voting; stronger inference-time baselines (e.g., self-consistency variants, chain-of-thought aggregation) are absent
Zhang et al. (2026) is the foundational motivation paper yet appears to be a concurrent or future work — the dependence on this single anchor weakens independent contribution framing
Scaling behavior described as 'monotonically with K' lacks any ablation showing diminishing returns or cost analysis at large K

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction follows a near-perfect formulaic template: problem statement → two-category prior work taxonomy → 'our key insight' pivot sentence → method description → exactly three bullet contributions. This rigid tripartite structure, the 'Our key insight is that...' phrasing, and the absence of any digressive or nuanced authorial voice are strong indicators of LLM generation. The specificity of quantitative values (p = 1.14e-5) adds surface texture but does not offset the structural uniformity.
